cards.text: Grab your apron, friend: in First John, the writer has just shown his readers how to tell the children of God from the children of the devil (1 John 3:10). Now he goes back to the message they've heard from the very beginning. Not new, not trendy, this recipe is OLDER than my mustache, and friend, this mustache has SEEN things.

cards.question: What's the message the writer's readers have heard from the beginning?

cards.text: The writer says don't be like Cain, Adam and Eve's son (Genesis 4:1), who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. Then the writer asks the big question himself: why'd Cain do it?

cards.question: The writer says Cain killed his brother because Cain's own deeds were ___, while his brother's deeds were ___.

cards.text: Then the writer turns to his readers and calls them brothers. He gives them a heads-up about how the world might treat them.

cards.question: True or false: The writer tells his brothers they should expect the world to love them.

cards.text: The writer says we know we've passed from death to life. And he says EXACTLY how we know it.

cards.question: The writer says we know we've passed from death to life because we ___ our brothers.

cards.text: The writer adds that the one who does not love remains in death. Then he turns to anyone who hates his brother, and he has a name for that person.

cards.question: What does the writer call everyone who hates his brother?

cards.text: And the writer says you know eternal life does not reside in a murderer. That's a heavy line, friend.
So what does real love actually look like? The writer says we can know it, and he points straight to Jesus.

cards.question: How does the writer say we know what love is?

answers.text: Jesus laid down His life for us
Jesus wrote it on stone tablets
Jesus showed it to us in a vision

cards.question: True or false: The writer says we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.

cards.text: Then the writer gets practical: picture someone with earthly possessions who sees his brother in need and withholds his compassion. That's me with a FULL cookie box, watching my friend go without, slowly closing the lid while we make eye contact.

cards.question: The writer asks a question about the person who sees his brother in need and won't show compassion. What does he ask?

answers.text: How can the love of God abide in him
Why didn't his brother ask sooner
Who will pay his brother back

cards.text: Now the writer calls his readers little children and boils this whole thing down to one line about how love should show up. ONE line, friend, and I've got a sugar cookie recipe that needs a whole index card front AND back.

cards.question: How does the writer tell his little children to love?

cards.text: Love in word only is me yelling "I GOT YOU, friend, ANYTHING you need!" and then ducking behind the oven the second forty empty cookie boxes roll in. Then the writer says that by this we will know something about what we belong to.

cards.question: True or false: Right after telling his little children to love in action and truth, the writer says that by this we will know that we belong to the world.

cards.text: The writer says we will assure our hearts in His presence, even if our hearts condemn us. Some days my heart goes off like a smoke alarm screaming over ONE cookie that's barely golden, and the writer has something to remember about God for exactly those days.

cards.question: Even if our hearts condemn us, what does the writer say about God?

answers.text: God is greater than our hearts
God stays far from our hearts

cards.text: And God knows all things. Friend, back when I sat forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, my heart said a LOT about me, none of it nice, and God is greater than every single word of it.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says if our hearts do not condemn us, we should still be afraid before God.
The writer says we will receive from God whatever we ask. Why?

answers.text: We keep His commandments and do what pleases Him
We ask Him again and again until He says yes
We give Him a tenth of everything we earn

cards.text: The writer says we keep God's commandments, and now he spells out His commandment in two parts. Part two you already know by heart, friend: love one another, just as He commanded us.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says part one of God's commandment is that we should believe in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ.

cards.text: The writer says, "Whoever keeps His commandments remains in God, and God in him." REMAINS, friend, not grabbing one cookie and hollering "Can't stay long!" from the doorway, and the writer tells us how we can know God remains in us.

cards.question: How does the writer say we know God remains in us?

answers.text: By the Spirit God has given us
By the signs God shows us each day
By the dreams God gives us at night
